title: Lift gemm_axpy_into_view with small-prime SIMD fast path (026fc832 Phase 6 prereq)
description:
Phase 6 architectural prerequisite under epic `026fc832`. Wave-6 design reviews uncovered that `gemm_axpy_into_view` (used by all `trsm_*` kernels and by the existing `rref` back-substitution path) does NOT dispatch the small-prime AVX2 whole-GEMM fast path. Currently it does per-cell `dot_product_slices`, which only routes the medium-prime u16 packed dot for primes 252-65521; for small primes ($P \le 251$) it falls back to scalar. The whole-GEMM small-prime kernel `fp_small_try_gemm_classical` is reachable only via `gemm()`'s dispatch. This blocks the Phase 6 echelon (`24a93e4e` design / `869ce43b` impl) and invert (`feb15da9` design / `8df0c501` impl) routes from inheriting the small-prime fast path through TRSM. The user-approved decision (session 6, 2026-05-25) is to **lift** `gemm_axpy_into_view` to dispatch the small-prime fast path, so all current and future TRSM-style code inherits the speedup. ## Background Current dispatch: - `gemm()` (`crates/gf2-core/src/field/matrix.rs:2642`): calls `F::try_simd_gemm_classical()` → `fp_small_try_gemm_classical` for $P \le 251$, packed u16 dot for $252 \le P \le 65521$. **Has small-prime fast path.** - `gemm_axpy_into_view` (`crates/gf2-core/src/field/matrix.rs:2854-2920`): per-cell loop over `dot_product_slices`. `dot_product_slices` (`crates/gf2-core/src/field/vec.rs:480-492`) calls `F::try_fp_simd_dot_product()` which only routes medium-prime u16 packed dot. **Missing small-prime fast path.** - `trsm_lower` (`crates/gf2-core/src/field/triangular.rs:751`) and `trsm_upper` (line 692) both call `gemm_axpy_into_view`. Therefore TRSM inherits the gap. ## Scope Extend `gemm_axpy_into_view` to dispatch a whole-GEMM small-prime fast path. Two implementation strategies are acceptable: 1. **Scratch-buffer + add-into-view:** When `F::try_simd_gemm_classical` is available, allocate a scratch FieldMatrix of the output shape, call `fp_small_try_gemm_classical` into it, then add-into-view the existing destination with the alpha/beta semantics. One allocation per call. 2. **Direct fused alpha-beta panel kernel:** Add a new SSOT helper `fp_small_try_gemm_axpy_classical

` that computes `C = alpha * A * B + beta * C` directly. Avoid the scratch allocation. Larger implementation but cleaner. Implementation choice is the impl agent's call; both must produce bit-exact results. ## Success Criteria - [hard] `gemm_axpy_into_view` for `Fp

` with $P \le 251$ reaches `fp_small_try_gemm_classical` (or its alpha-beta variant) when `simd` feature is enabled and AVX2 is available at runtime. - [hard] No regression on existing call sites (`trsm_lower`, `trsm_upper`, the recursive PLE Schur-update path) at any (prime, n) cell currently PASSing post-`41096af5` (delta ≤ 5%). - [hard] Bit-exact correctness preserved across all primes (proptest sweep at boundary lengths {0, 1, 15, 16, 17, 63, 64, 65} for $p \in \{7, 31, 127, 241, 251, 65521\}$). - [hard] Unsafe stays in `gf2-kernels-simd` (no new unsafe code in `gf2-core`). - [hard] No BLAS dependency; pure Rust + AVX2. - [hard] After this task lands, `trsm_lower` + `trsm_upper` at GF(7)/256, GF(251)/256, GF(65521)/256 exhibit measurable speedup over their pre-lift performance (the lift is verified empirically — a 5-trial CCX1-pinned micro-bench in `dev/bench_results/`). - [hard] Test coverage explicitly exercises the `gemm_axpy_into_view` small-prime path (a new `#[test]` calls into the function with `Fp<251>` and verifies bit-exact equality vs the existing scalar oracle at n ∈ {16, 64, 256}). ## Out of scope - The downstream echelon (`869ce43b`), invert (`8df0c501`), solve (`6613abf4`) impls (separate tasks). - AVX-512 (epic `7f809931`). - Mersenne31 dispatch through `gemm_axpy_into_view` (separate task if needed; current Mersenne31 echelon stays scalar). ## Notes - Filed session 6 (2026-05-25) after wave-6 review uncovered the dispatch gap. - All wave 7a/7b implementation tasks (`6823c8a0`, `869ce43b`, `8df0c501`, `6613abf4`) become dependents of this task.
